title: NY State Senate · District 28
area: Manhattan's East Side, including the Upper East Side, Yorkville, Midtown East, Murray Hill, Kips Bay, and Gramercy.

context.text: Incumbent Liz Krueger (D) advanced without a primary opponent; Alina Bonsell (R, Block Mamdani Party) also advanced without a primary opponent. Krueger is not running on the Working Families Party line this cycle.

candidates.name: Liz Krueger
candidates.currentRole: New York State Senator, District 28 (since 2013); previously District 26 (2002-2013)

summary.text: Liz Krueger is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election to NY Senate District 28. First elected in a 2002 special election, she chairs the powerful Senate Finance Committee and has focused on tax and budget policy, affordable housing, reproductive health, climate legislation, and hunger/anti-poverty programs.

background.text: Earned a B.S. in social policy/human development from Northwestern University (1979) and an M.A. in public policy from the University of Chicago (1981).

Was the founding director of the New York City Food Bank and worked in hunger/anti-poverty roles, including as Special Project Coordinator for the Greater Cleveland Community Food Bank and Associate Director for the Community Food Resources Center.
First ran for the State Senate in 2000, narrowly losing to incumbent Republican Roy Goodman; won the seat in a 2002 special election after Goodman resigned.

Elected Chair of the Senate Finance Committee after Democrats won the Senate majority in 2018, one of the most powerful posts in the chamber; also sits on the Budget and Revenue and Rules committees in 2025-2026.

priorities.text: Tax and government reform: modernizing New York State's governmental processes, electoral system, and tax policy.
Healthcare and reproductive rights, including leadership on the Reproductive Health Act and postpartum depression legislation.
Protecting and expanding affordable housing and addressing homelessness.
Climate and environmental policy, including the Climate Change Superfund Act, a fracking ban, a plastic bag ban, and fossil-fuel divestment from state pension funds.
Hunger and anti-poverty policy, including expanding SNAP access and opposing federal cuts to food assistance.

positions.summary: Official biography credits her with passing the Climate Change Superfund Act, helping lead the effort to ban fracking in New York, and working on a plan to divest the state pension fund from fossil fuels; she also sponsors the Solar UP Now NY Act, which removes regulatory barriers to small plug-in solar devices.
Cited as a leader on New York's Reproductive Health Act and related reproductive-health legislation.

record.text: Chairs the Senate Finance Committee, a post she has held since 2019; also serves on the Budget and Revenue and Rules committees in the 2025-2026 session.

Sponsored S8512C, the Solar UP Now NY Act, creating a regulatory framework for portable solar generation devices and exempting them from interconnection/net-metering requirements; passed the Senate 62-0 on April 21, 2026 and was substituted by Assembly companion A9111C, which passed the Assembly 59-1 on May 28, 2026.
Joined 69 state lawmakers in a September 2026 letter urging New York's congressional delegation to reverse federal SNAP cuts.
Publicly opposed proposals to shift the cost of new nuclear power plants onto utility ratepayers and taxpayers.

summary.text: Alina Bonsell is the Republican and Block Mamdani Party nominee challenging incumbent Liz Krueger. A 20-year East Side resident and a Jewish refugee from the former Soviet Union who came to the U.S. as a child, she works in the pharmaceutical/biotech and private sectors and previously ran unsuccessfully for New York City Council District 5 in 2025.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Hofstra University.
Has approximately 20 years of professional experience in the pharmaceutical, biotech, and healthcare private sectors.
background.quote: 20 years of experience in pharmaceutical, biotech, healthcare, and the private sector, where results matter, and accountability is non-negotiable

background.text: Ran for New York City Council District 5 in 2025 on the Republican line and lost to incumbent Julie Menin, 73.7% to 26.0%.
Came to the United States as a child when her family fled the Soviet Union as Jewish refugees.

priorities.text: Restore public safety by repealing bail reform, enforcing quality-of-life laws, and giving law enforcement more tools and support.
priorities.quote: Bail reform has failed! Repeat offenders cycle through the system while law-abiding residents pay the price. It's time to repeal these policies, restore accountability, and give law enforcement the support and tools they need to do their jobs.

priorities.text: Cut government waste and fraud and return savings as targeted tax relief, including exempting young professionals and single working parents from certain state taxes and protecting 401(k) withdrawals from state taxation up to cost-of-living thresholds.
priorities.quote: New York has a spending problem, not a revenue problem. The answer isn't to tax more, it's to govern better.

priorities.text: Promote economic growth and innovation, including lifting the fracking ban, opposing shutdowns of data centers, repealing congestion pricing, and expanding charter schools.
priorities.quote: Lift the fracking ban. Stop shutting down data centers. Repeal the congestion tax. Expand charter schools so every parent has a choice, not just those zoned for failing schools.

priorities.text: Reform family court and address neighborhood overdevelopment and shelter-placement policy.

positions.summary: Her Ballotpedia survey response lists "more police" among her local priorities.
positions.quote: cleaner and safer streets with more police

positions.summary: Campaign principles page lists support for charter school expansion.
Campaign plan calls for easing building restrictions under housing incentive programs to encourage more construction.
positions.quote: ease building restrictions under housing incentive programs to encourage more construction

positions.summary: Campaign plan calls for removing long-term vacant units that need extensive capital rehabilitation from rent stabilization.
positions.quote: Remove long-term vacant units from rent stabilization constraints if they require extensive capital rehabilitation to meet legal human-occupancy standards.

positions.summary: Campaign principles page lists a woman's right to choose among her principles.
Campaign plan supports cost-effective solar, wind and storage projects alongside nuclear power and a review of the fracking ban, and criticizes a $200 million Senate allocation for solar.
positions.quote: The State Senate’s recent $200 million infrastructure allocation for solar energy is an inefficient waste of taxpayer money

researchNotes: Krueger's positions are drawn from her official Senate bio and press releases rather than a campaign website with an explicit platform; some commonly attributed positions (e.g., on congestion pricing or immigration) could not be confirmed with a direct citable statement and were left out rather than inferred from party.
